paper.title: Accelerating Linear Bandits with Persistent Candidate Sets

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandit with a fixed finite action set
unmapped: noise R-sub-Gaussian conditionally on history and selected action
settings.definition_quote: We consider a stochastic linear bandit with a fixed finite action set indexed by $[K]=\{1,\ldots,K\}$. Each action $i$ has a known feature vector $x_i\in\R^d$ ... We assume $\lVert x_i\rVert_2\le L$, $\lVert\theta^\star\rVert_2\le S$, and $\mu_i\in[-1,1]$ for every action. ... $\eta_t$ is conditionally $R$-sub-Gaussian given the history before round $t$ and the selected action $I_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandit with uniform challenger sampling policy class (lower bound)
unmapped: policies restricted to maintain k active actions and sample q challengers uniformly from the remaining K-k actions; may only play / retain actions in the candidate set
holds even if identity of optimal action is known
settings.definition_quote: Consider a general class of policies that maintain $k$ active actions and sample $q$ challengers uniformly from the remaining $K-k$ actions at each round. The union of the active and challenger sets forms the candidate set, from which the policy must choose both the played action and the next active set.

symbols.beta_r: confidence radius R*sqrt(d*log(1+T L^2/(lam d)) + 2 log(1/delta)) + sqrt(lam)*S
symbols.q: number of challengers sampled per round
symbols.delta_p: second failure probability delta' for the discovery term

tuning: beta set as in Eq. (confidence-radius) with confidence delta

source.label: thm:problem-independent-regret
source.quote: Fix $T\ge 2$, $\delta,\delta'\in(0,1)$, $1\le k<K$, and $1\le q\le K-k$, and let $\beta$ be defined by Eq.~\eqref{eq:confidence-radius}. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta-\delta'$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:persistent-candidate} satisfies R_T \le 2\max\{\beta,1\}\sqrt{2Td\log(1+\frac{TL^2}{\lambda d})} + 2\lceil\frac{K-k}{q}(\log(K-k)+\log\frac{1}{\delta'})\rceil.

results.notes: Holds with probability >= 1 - delta - delta'. R_T is the pathwise pseudo-regret sum of gaps. Paper's L is L_feat, R is sigma.

symbols.q: number of challengers sampled per round

tuning: beta set as in Eq. (confidence-radius) with confidence delta

source.label: thm:problem-dependent-regret
source.quote: Under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:problem-independent-regret}, with probability at least $1-\delta-\delta'$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:persistent-candidate} satisfies R_T \le \frac{8\max\{\beta^2,1\}d}{\Delta_{\min}}\log(1+\frac{TL^2}{\lambda d}) + 2\lceil\frac{K-k}{q}(\log(K-k)+\log\frac{1}{\delta'})\rceil.

symbols.q: number of challengers sampled per round

conditions: unique optimal action which is initially inactive

source.label: thm:uniform-gating-lower-bound
source.quote: Suppose the optimal action $i^\star$ is unique and initially inactive. Then, for every $T\ge1$, every policy in this class satisfies \E[R_T^{\mathrm{access}}] = \Delta\frac{K-k-q}{q}[1-(1-\frac{q}{K-k})^T].

results.notes: Exact expression for the expected access-induced regret Delta*sum_t 1{tau>t}, where Delta = min gap; since R_T >= R_T^access pathwise, it lower-bounds expected pseudo-regret for policies in the uniform-challenger class.

symbols.q: number of challengers sampled per round

conditions: unique optimal action which is initially inactive
results.notes: Stated for expected access-induced regret; transfers to expected pseudo-regret E[R_T] via the pathwise inequality R_T >= R_T^access (explicit in the proof). Delta is the minimum gap.
